Calculate sample size to detect at least one case

Source: R/design_detection.R
design_detection.Rd

Given the expected true prevalence of a (possibly rare) variant or condition, returns the number of people needed so that the chance of finding at least one case reaches a target (detection_prob). Supply n instead to run it in reverse: the function then reports the chance of finding at least one case with that many people.

Three design modes – controlled by n_sites and n_per_site:

Unclustered (n_sites = NULL, n_per_site = NULL)

Returns the number of people.

Fixed site size (n_per_site supplied)

Solves for the number of sites.

Fixed number of sites (n_sites supplied)

Solves for the number of people per site.

Usage

design_detection(
  prevalence,
  detection_prob = 0.8,
  n = NULL,
  sensitivity = 1,
  n_sites = NULL,
  n_per_site = NULL,
  icc = 0
)

Arguments

prevalence

Expected true prevalence, in (0, 1): the lowest prevalence the study should be able to detect.

detection_prob

Target chance of finding at least one case, in (0, 1); default 0.80. Not used when n is supplied.

n

Optional whole number. If supplied, the function runs in reverse and reports the chance of finding at least one case among n people.

sensitivity

Diagnostic sensitivity in (0, 1]; default 1 (the test never misses a case).

n_sites

Optional whole number. Fixes the number of sites; the function solves for people per site. Cannot be used with n_per_site.

n_per_site

Optional whole number. Fixes the number of people per site; the function solves for the number of sites. Cannot be used with n_sites.

icc

Intra-cluster correlation, in [0, 1); default 0 (no clustering). An icc above 0 needs n_sites or n_per_site.

Value

A list with:

n

Total sample size (or n as supplied, in reverse). With sites, n_sites * n_per_site.

n_sites

Number of sites (NULL if unclustered).

n_per_site

People per site (NULL if unclustered).

deff

Design effect: n divided by the number of people with no clustering who give the same chance of finding a case; 1 if unclustered.

n_eff

Number of people needed with no clustering, \(n_0\) rounded up (in reverse, the number with no clustering who give the same chance of finding a case).

detection_prob

The target (forward), or the chance achieved with n people (reverse).

Details

Sample size. Each person tested has a chance \(q = prevalence \times sensitivity\) of being a true case whom the test detects. The chance that no case is found among \(n\) people is \((1 - q)^n\), so the number of people needed is

$$n_0 = \frac{\log(1 - detection\_prob)}{\log(1 - q)}$$

rounded up (Cannon 2001, equation 4.6). Positives are assumed to be confirmed, for example by a second test (Cannon 2001), so a false positive is not counted as finding a case, and specificity is not used.

Clustering. Cases bunch together at sites, so the chance \(q\) is taken to vary between sites as a beta distribution with mean \(q\) and intra-cluster correlation ICC, as in DRpower. The chance that no case is found among \(m\) people at one site is

$$P_0(m) = \frac{B(\alpha, \beta + m)}{B(\alpha, \beta)}, \qquad \alpha = q \left(\frac{1}{ICC} - 1\right), \quad \beta = (1 - q) \left(\frac{1}{ICC} - 1\right),$$

and at \(k\) sites it is \(P_0(m)^k\). With n_per_site fixed, the number of sites is \(\lceil \log(1 - detection\_prob) / \log P_0(n_{per site}) \rceil\). With n_sites fixed there is no formula for the people per site, so the smallest whole number that reaches detection_prob is found by a numerical search. \(P_0(m)\) always falls towards 0 as \(m\) grows, but very slowly when the ICC is high and cases are rare; if even \(10^{15}\) people per site fall short, the function stops.

Sites and rounding. With n_sites fixed, every site is used, with at least 1 person each, even if fewer people would do (as in the other design functions). A site larger than needed gives 1 site of that size. With sites, the returned n is the number actually sampled, n_sites * n_per_site.

References

Cannon, R. M. (2001) Sense and sensitivity: designing surveys based on an imperfect test. Preventive Veterinary Medicine 49(3-4), 141-163. doi:10.1016/S0167-5877(01)00184-2 (Section 4.)

Verity, R. & Ruybal, S. DRpower: Study design and analysis for pfhrp2/3 deletion prevalence studies. R package version 1.0.4 (functions get_power_presence() and get_sample_size_presence()). https://github.com/mrc-ide/DRpower

MMS-SD Study Design Workshop, Module 7. https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMS-SD_workshop/

Examples

# 80 percent chance of finding a case at 5 percent prevalence
design_detection(prevalence = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 32
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 32
#> 
#> $detection_prob
#> [1] 0.8
#> 

# Imperfect test
design_detection(prevalence = 0.05, sensitivity = 0.8)
#> $n
#> [1] 40
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 40
#> 
#> $detection_prob
#> [1] 0.8
#> 

# Reverse: the chance of finding a 1 percent variant with 139 people
design_detection(prevalence = 0.01, n = 139)
#> $n
#> [1] 139
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 139
#> 
#> $detection_prob
#> [1] 0.7526613
#> 

# Fixed site size: how many sites?
design_detection(prevalence = 0.05, n_per_site = 10, icc = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 40
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1.223414
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 32
#> 
#> $detection_prob
#> [1] 0.8
#> 

# Fixed number of sites: how many people per site?
design_detection(prevalence = 0.01, n_sites = 5, icc = 0.1)
#> $n
#> [1] 1470
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 294
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 9.17942
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 161
#> 
#> $detection_prob
#> [1] 0.8
#>
